payload.text: I used to believe that working the field alone was effective and sufficient for fieldwork. I now prefer paired transects twice a month, with the rest of the season conducted solo for analysis. A second observer catches my drift before it becomes a published error, and being alone for a whole season quietly wrecks my judgment. This shift occurred because of firsthand experience showing that solitude leads to judgment errors, and having a second observer improves accuracy and prevents mistakes from going unnoticed.
